subject: HID: nintendo: skip baudrate setup for 8BitDo adapters
author: Michał Kopeć
provenance_doc_ref: none -- postdates docs/patch-provenance.md's baseline; first mention is docs/kernel-recon/fork-sync-2026-09/PLAN.md Sec 2.10.

impact.effect_if_absent: An 8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter switched to Switch mode presents as a genuine Nintendo Switch Pro Controller (057e:2009, USB_DEVICE_ID_NINTENDO_PROCON) and is claimed by hid-nintendo. hid-nintendo's probe path unconditionally sends JC_USB_CMD_BAUDRATE_3M after a successful USB handshake; the adapter does not implement that command and enters an error state, disconnecting and re-enumerating in a tight loop (measured 17x on the author's hardware, ~512ms apart, 13x 'Failed to set baudrate (ret=-71)', 13x 'Failed handshake; ret=-71', 18x 'probe - fail'). Probe never completes, no input device is created, and because a specialised driver (hid-nintendo) still matches the ID table, hid_generic_match() declines to bind hid-generic either -- the HID device is left bound to nothing. The gamepad is unusable; the wired/paired controller behind the adapter produces no input at all.
affected_hardware: 8BitDo USB Wireless Adapter (1st generation), in Switch mode, presenting as 057e:2009
any 8BitDo controller paired through that adapter (author tested an SN30 Pro+)
impact.failure_mode: loud-in-dmesg-silent-to-user -- kernel log fills with repeated 'Failed to set baudrate', 'Failed handshake', and USB disconnect/reconnect messages (loud, but only visible over a serial console or `dmesg`, which a MiSTer user at the OSD never sees), while the user-facing symptom is simply 'the gamepad does not work' with no on-screen diagnostic -- Main_MiSTer has no code path that surfaces a failed HID bind. Graded 'loud' per the schema's two-value axis because the failure is not silent at the kernel level (errors are logged, the device visibly re-enumerates) -- picking 'silent' would hide the fact that `dmesg` already contains the exact signature (13x -EPROTO/-71, 18x 'probe - fail') needed to diagnose this without re-deriving anything, which is the operationally relevant distinction for this schema field.

userspace_coupling.interface: evdev VID:PID + idstr matching on the Nintendo Switch controller family (057e:2xxx), which only exists once hid-nintendo has bound the device and created an input node
userspace_coupling.main_mister_ref: $S/main/input.cpp:2752 `else if (input[dev].vid == 0x057e && ((input[dev].pid & 0xFF00) == 0x2000))` (the '// nintendo switch controllers' LED block, covers 057e:2009); input.cpp:4733-4734 `strcpy(input[l].idstr, "057e_2009"); strcpy(input[r].idstr, "057e_2009");` inside check_joycon()'s combo-detection path; input.cpp:5309 `else if (!strcasestr(input[n].name, "Pro Controller"))` gates WIIMOTE-quirk handling off the reported device name hid-nintendo assigns. Two further 8BitDo-specific paths exist at input.cpp:5852 ('Menu combo on 8BitDo receiver in PSC mode', vid 0x054c/pid 0x0cda) and input.cpp:6130 ('Menu button on 8BitDo Receiver in D-Input mode', vid 0x2dc8/pid 0x3100|0x3104) -- those are a *different* 8BitDo product (a dedicated USB receiver dongle with its own VID:PID, not the Switch-mode adapter this commit targets, which spoofs Nintendo's own 057e:2009) and do not themselves depend on hid-nintendo; they are cited here only because the plan's grep list named them, and to avoid conflating the two 8BitDo device classes. coupled=true rests on the 057e:2xxx paths: without hid-nintendo binding the adapter, no evdev device with vid=0x057e/pid=0x2009 is created at all, so none of input.cpp's Nintendo-family code (LED mapping, joycon combining, DPAD simulation, WIIMOTE-quirk exclusion) ever runs for this hardware -- the gamepad is invisible to Main_MiSTer, not merely misbehaving.

forward_port.effort: small -- 20/-12 lines, self-contained reorder plus one new inline helper. Measured directly: applied the eight patches that already touch drivers/hid/hid-nintendo.c in our de10nano stack (0015, 0032, 0034, 0035, 0038, 0039, 0040, 0041, in that numeric order, `patch -p1 -F0`) to $S/linux's v6.18.49 hid-nintendo.c, then applied this PR's diff on top with `patch -p1 -F0`: all eight prerequisite patches applied clean (0015 took a -4 line offset on hunk 5, the other seven zero offset/zero fuzz), and the PR #92 diff then applied clean with offsets only (hunk 1 +20, hunk 2 +70, hunk 3 +70 lines) and zero fuzz/zero rejects. Repeated against v7.2.3's hid-nintendo.c ($S/linux-7.2, matching the beta series' hid-nintendo patches -- 0015 is a real re-anchored copy in linux-patches-beta/, the other seven are symlinks to the de10nano originals, confirmed by `ls -la`): same eight patches applied clean (0015 offset -4 on hunk 5; 0032 offsets 20/21/27/27; 0034 offsets 20/20; 0035 offset 27; 0038 offset 24; 0039 offset 20; 0040 offset 24; 0041 offsets 27/27 -- all offset-only, zero fuzz, matching the beta series file's own header note about 0038-0041's apply history), and PR #92's diff then applied clean with offsets only (hunk 1 +40, hunk 2 +91, hunk 3 +91) and zero fuzz/zero rejects. No conflict with any of our eight carried hid-nintendo hunks on either kernel.

license_provenance: GPL-2.0 (same license as drivers/hid/hid-nintendo.c). Original patch posted to linux-input on 2025-07-20 by Michal Kopec (Link: lore.kernel.org/linux-input/20250720143156.2563816-1-michal.kopec@3mdeb.com/), received no upstream review. Landed on MiSTer-v6.18 as PR #92 carrying Michal Kopec's original authorship in the commit's `Author:` field but with no Signed-off-by from him -- the commit message states explicitly 'This commit carries no Signed-off-by from the original author, who has not been asked to certify it -- it is submitted here by the tester', Tested-by/Signed-off-by Kasper Solesen. This is a gap our carried patch inherits: we can carry the code (GPL-2.0, same as the file it patches) but the DCO chain for the original author is incomplete upstream, and that status does not change by our carrying it -- worth flagging if this patch is ever proposed back to mainline rather than just carried downstream.
